title.en: Volume 189 Biographies 77: Li Wenxiang, Sun Pan, Hu Guan, Luo Qiao, Ye Zhao, Dai Guan, Huang Gong, Lu Zhen, Xia Liangsheng, He Zun
title.raw: 卷一百八十九 列傳第七十七 李文祥 孫磐 胡爟 羅僑 葉釗 戴冠 黃鞏 陸震 夏良勝 何遵 Volume 189 Biographies 77: Li Wenxiang, Sun Pan, Hu Guan, Luo Qiao, Ye Zhao, Dai Guan, Huang Gong, Lu Zhen, Xia Liangsheng, He Zun

sentences.zh: 【列傳第七十七李文祥·孫磐·徐珪·胡爟·周時從·王雄·羅僑·葉釗·劉天麒·戴冠·黃鞏·陸震·夏良勝·萬潮等·何遵·劉校等】

translations.literal: Biographies 77: Li Wenxiang, Sun Pan, Xu Gui, Hu Guan, Zhou Shicong, Wang Xiong, Luo Qiao, Ye Zhao, Liu Tianqi, Dai Guan, Huang Gong, Lu Zhen, Xia Liangsheng, Wan Chao and others, He Zun, Liu Xiao and others
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 77: Li Wenxiang, Sun Pan, Xu Gui, Hu Guan, Zhou Shicong, Wang Xiong, Luo Qiao, Ye Zhao, Liu Tianqi, Dai Guan, Huang Gong, Lu Zhen, Xia Liangsheng, Wan Chao and others, He Zun, Liu Xiao and others So it was.

sentences.zh: 李文祥，字天瑞，麻城人。

translations.literal: Li Wenxiang, styled Tianrui, was a man of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenxiang, styled Tianrui, was a native of Macheng.

sentences.zh: 祖正芳，山西布政使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhengfang was Shanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhengfang served as Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 父，陝西參政。

translations.literal: His father was Shaanxi Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father served as Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 文祥自幼俊異。

translations.literal: Wenxiang from youth was outstanding and exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang was precocious and outstanding from childhood.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉于鄉，成化末登進士。

translations.literal: At weak crown he was selected in the prefecture; at the end of Chenghua he attained jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: At age twenty he passed the provincial examination, and at the end of the Chenghua reign he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 萬安當國，重其才。

translations.literal: Wan An held the state; he valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan An held power, he valued Wenxiang's talent.

sentences.zh: 以孫弘璧與同榜，款于家，文祥意弗慊也。

translations.literal: Because Sun Hongbi was of the same examination list, Wan entertained him at home; Wenxiang's mind was not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sun Hongbi had passed the jinshi examination in the same year, Wan entertained him at home, and Wenxiang was displeased.

sentences.zh: 屬題畫鳩，語含刺，安深銜之。

translations.literal: Assigned to inscribe a painting of turtledoves, his words contained barbs; An deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When assigned to inscribe a painting of turtledoves, his words carried satire, and Wan deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，孝宗嗣位，即上封事，略曰：

translations.literal: Before long, Xiaozong succeeded to the throne; he immediately submitted a sealed memorial, in summary saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when Emperor Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he immediately submitted a sealed memorial, in summary saying:

sentences.zh: 祖宗設內閣、六部，贊萬幾，理庶務，職至重也。

translations.literal: The ancestors established the Grand Secretariat and Six Ministries to assist the myriad affairs and manage common business—the office is extremely weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors established the Grand Secretariat and the Six Ministries to assist in the myriad duties of state and manage common affairs—a responsibility of the utmost weight.

sentences.zh: 頃者，在位多匪人，權移內侍。

translations.literal: Recently, those in office are mostly unworthy men; power has shifted to inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, many unworthy men have held office, and power has shifted to inner eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 賞罰任其喜怒，禍福聽其轉移。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments follow their joy and anger; fortune and disaster listen to their turning.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments follow their caprice; fortune and disaster depend on their whim.

sentences.zh: 仇視言官，公行賄賂。

translations.literal: They regard remonstrating officials with enmity and openly practice bribery.
translations.idiomatic: They treat remonstrating officials as enemies and openly accept bribes.

sentences.zh: 阿之則交引驟遷，忤之則巧讒遠竄。

translations.literal: Those who flatter them are promoted in rapid succession; those who oppose them are slandered by artifice and banished far away.
translations.idiomatic: Those who flatter them are rapidly promoted in succession, while those who oppose them are slandered by artifice and banished to distant posts.

sentences.zh: 朝野寒心，道路側目。

translations.literal: Court and countryside are chilled at heart; travelers on the road avert their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The court and the countryside are chilled with fear, and people on the roads avert their eyes.

sentences.zh: 望陛下密察渠魁，明彰國憲，擇謹厚者供使令。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will secretly investigate the ringleaders, clearly display the national statutes, and choose prudent and honest men to serve as attendants.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will secretly investigate the ringleaders, clearly enforce the national statutes, and choose prudent and honest men to serve as attendants.

sentences.zh: 更博選大臣，諮諏治理，推心委任，不復嫌疑，然後體統正而近習不得肆也。

translations.literal: Further, broadly select great ministers, consult on governance, entrust them with open hearts without further suspicion—then the institutional order will be correct and close associates cannot act wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Further, broadly select senior ministers, consult them on governance, and entrust them with open hearts free of suspicion—then the institutional order will be restored and close associates will no longer act wantonly.

sentences.zh: 祖宗定律，輕重適宜。

translations.literal: The ancestors established laws with punishments light and heavy suitably matched.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors established laws with punishments appropriately graded in severity.

sentences.zh: 頃法司專徇己私，不恤國典。

translations.literal: Recently the judicial offices have exclusively followed private interest, not caring for the national code.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the judicial offices have exclusively pursued private interest, heedless of the national code.

sentences.zh: 豪強者雖重必寬，貧弱者雖輕必罪。

translations.literal: The powerful and strong, though guilty of serious crimes, are surely treated leniently; the poor and weak, though guilty of light crimes, are surely punished.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful, though guilty of serious crimes, are invariably treated leniently, while the poor and weak, though guilty of minor offenses, are invariably punished.

sentences.zh: 惠及奸宄，養成玩俗。

translations.literal: Benefit reaches evil-doers and cultivates a playful custom.
translations.idiomatic: Evildoers are favored, and lax customs are cultivated.

sentences.zh: 兼之風尚奢麗，禮制蕩然。

translations.literal: Added to this, custom tends toward extravagant beauty and ritual systems are swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, customs have turned extravagant and ritual systems have collapsed.

sentences.zh: 豪民僭王者之居，富室擬公侯之服。

translations.literal: Overbearing commoners usurp the dwellings of kings; wealthy houses imitate the dress of dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Overbearing commoners build dwellings fit for kings, and wealthy households dress like dukes and marquises.

sentences.zh: 奇技淫巧，上下同流。

translations.literal: Strange skills and licentious crafts—above and below flow together.
translations.idiomatic: Strange skills and licentious crafts flow unchecked from top to bottom.

sentences.zh: 望陛下申明舊章，俾法曹遵律令，臣庶各守等威，然後禮法明而人心不敢玩也。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will clarify the old regulations, cause the legal officials to follow statutes and orders, and ministers and commoners each to keep their rank and authority—then ritual and law will be clear and people's hearts will not dare to treat them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will clarify the old regulations, require legal officials to follow statutes and orders, and require ministers and commoners each to observe their proper rank—then ritual and law will be clear and no one will dare treat them lightly.

sentences.zh: 然國無其人，誰與共理？

translations.literal: Yet if the state lacks such men, with whom shall we jointly govern?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the state lacks such men, with whom shall we govern together?

sentences.zh: 致仕尚書王恕、王竑，孤忠自許，齒力未衰；

translations.literal: Retired Minister Wang Su and Wang Hong, solitary in loyalty and self-assured, their teeth and strength not yet declined;
translations.idiomatic: Retired Ministers Wang Su and Wang Hong, steadfast in solitary loyalty, are still vigorous in age and strength;

sentences.zh: 南京主事林俊、思南通判王純，剛方植躬，才品兼茂。

translations.literal: Nanjing Section Chief Lin Jun and Sicuan Assistant Prefect Wang Chun of Sinan are upright in character and planted in self-cultivation, their talent and integrity both abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun, a section chief in Nanjing, and Wang Chun, assistant prefect of Sinan, are upright in character and of abundant talent and integrity.

sentences.zh: 望陛下起列朝端，資其議論，必有裨益，可翊明時。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will raise them to the court ranks and rely on their discourse—there will surely be benefit, able to assist the enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will summon them to court and rely on their counsel—they will surely be of benefit and can assist this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 且賢才難得，自古為然。

translations.literal: Moreover, worthy talent is hard to obtain—since ancient times it has been so.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, worthy talent is hard to obtain—as it has been since ancient times.

sentences.zh: 習俗移人，豪傑不免。

translations.literal: Custom shifts people; even heroes cannot avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Custom shifts people; even heroes cannot escape its influence.

sentences.zh: 惟茲臣庶，不盡庸愚。

translations.literal: Only among these ministers and commoners, not all are mediocre and foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among these officials and commoners, not all are mediocre and foolish.

sentences.zh: 能知自愧，即屬名流；

translations.literal: Those who can know shame belong to the ranks of the distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Those who can feel shame belong among the distinguished;

sentences.zh: 樂其危災，乃為猥品。

translations.literal: Those who rejoice in others' peril and disaster are base in character.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rejoice in others' misfortune are base in character.

sentences.zh: 願陛下明察群倫，罷其罔上營私違天蠹物者，餘則勉以自新。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty clearly to examine all ranks, dismiss those who deceive superiors, seek private gain, oppose Heaven, and harm things—let the rest be urged to renew themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty to examine all ranks clearly, dismiss those who deceive their superiors, seek private gain, oppose Heaven, and harm the commonwealth, and urge the rest to reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 既開改過之路，必多遷善之人。

translations.literal: Once the path of correcting faults is opened, there will surely be many who turn toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Once the path of repentance is opened, many will surely turn toward goodness.

sentences.zh: 臣見登極詔書，不許風聞言事。

translations.literal: Your servant sees in the accession edict that hearsay remonstrance is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant notes that the accession edict forbids remonstrance based on hearsay.

sentences.zh: 古聖王懸鼓設木，自求誹謗。

translations.literal: Ancient sage kings hung drums and set up posts, seeking slander themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage kings hung drums and set up posts, actively seeking criticism and slander.

sentences.zh: 言之縱非其情，聽者亦足為戒，何害于國，遽欲罪之？

translations.literal: Even if what is said does not match the facts, the listener can still take it as a warning—what harm to the state, that you hasten to punish it?
translations.idiomatic: Even if what is said does not match the facts, the listener can still take it as a warning—what harm does it do the state that you hasten to punish it?

sentences.zh: 昔李林甫持此以禍唐，王安石持此以禍宋。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Linfu relied on this to bring calamity on Tang; Wang Anshi relied on this to bring calamity on Song.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Li Linfu used this policy to bring calamity upon Tang; Wang Anshi used it to bring calamity upon Song.

sentences.zh: 遠近驟聞，莫不驚駭。

translations.literal: Near and far suddenly heard it; none were not startled and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far, all who heard it were startled and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 願陛下再頒明詔，廣求直言，庶不墮奸謀，足彰聖德。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty again to issue a clear edict, broadly seeking straight speech—then you will not fall into treacherous schemes and can fully display sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty to issue a clear edict again, broadly seeking frank remonstrance—you will not fall into treacherous schemes and will fully display sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 大率君子之言決非小人之利，諮問倘及，必肆中傷。

translations.literal: Generally, the words of gentlemen are certainly not to the profit of petty men; if consultation reaches them, they will surely launch slander at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Generally speaking, the words of gentlemen certainly do not serve the interests of petty men; if consultation reaches them, they will surely launch slander at the center.

sentences.zh: 如有所疑，請試面對。

translations.literal: If there is doubt, please try facing them directly.
translations.idiomatic: If there is doubt, please try confronting them face to face.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，宦官及執政萬安、劉吉、尹直等鹹惡之，數日不下。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, eunuchs and the ruling ministers Wan An, Liu Ji, Yin Zhi and others all hated it; for several days it was not issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, eunuchs and the ruling ministers Wan An, Liu Ji, Yin Zhi, and others all hated it, and for several days it was not forwarded.

sentences.zh: 忽詔詣左順門，以疏內有「中興再造」語，傳旨詰責。

translations.literal: Suddenly an edict summoned him to the Left Shun Gate; because within the memorial were the words 'restoring the state and rebuilding,' an imperial order was transmitted to question and rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he was summoned by edict to the Left Shun Gate; because the memorial contained the phrase 'restoring the state and rebuilding,' an imperial order was issued to question and rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 文祥從容辨析而出。

translations.literal: Wenxiang calmly analyzed and argued and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang calmly analyzed and argued his case and was released.

sentences.zh: 謫授陝西咸寧丞。

translations.literal: He was demoted and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xianning in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted and appointed assistant magistrate of Xianning in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 南京主事夏崇文論救，不納。

translations.literal: Nanjing Section Chief Xia Chongwen remonstrated in his defense; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Chongwen, a section chief in Nanjing, remonstrated in his defense, but the appeal was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 工部主事莆田林沂復請召文祥及湯鼐，納崇文言，且召陳獻章、謝鐸等。

translations.literal: Works Section Chief Lin Yi of Putian again requested summoning Wenxiang and Tang Nai, accepting Chongwen's words, and also summoning Chen Xianzhang, Xie Duo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi, a works section chief from Putian, again requested that Wenxiang and Tang Nai be summoned, that Chongwen's appeal be accepted, and that Chen Xianzhang, Xie Duo, and others also be summoned.

sentences.zh: 時安已去，吉、直激帝怒，嚴旨切責之。

translations.literal: At the time An had already departed; Ji and Zhi incited the emperor's anger and issued stern orders sharply rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wan An had already departed; Liu Ji and Yin Zhi incited the emperor's anger and issued stern orders sharply rebuking them.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多薦文祥，率為吉、直所沮。

translations.literal: Many court ministers recommended Wenxiang, but mostly they were obstructed by Ji and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Many court ministers recommended Wenxiang, but their efforts were mostly obstructed by Liu Ji and Yin Zhi.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年以王恕薦召為兵部主事，監司以下饋贐皆不納。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, on Wang Su's recommendation he was summoned as a section chief in the Ministry of War; gifts from supervising officials and below he all refused.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 2 (1489), on Wang Su's recommendation he was summoned to serve as a section chief in the Ministry of War; he refused all gifts from supervising officials and below.

sentences.zh: 到官未逾月，復以吉人事下獄，貶貴州興隆衛經歷。

translations.literal: Having taken office not yet a month, again on Ji's matter he was imprisoned and demoted to Administrator of Xinglong Guard in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month after taking office, he was again imprisoned on Liu Ji's account and demoted to administrator of Xinglong Guard in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 都御史鄧廷瓚征苗，咨以兵事，大奇之，欲薦為監司。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Deng Tingzan campaigning against the Miao consulted him on military affairs, greatly marveling at him and wishing to recommend him as a supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Deng Tingzan, campaigning against the Miao, consulted him on military affairs, greatly admired him, and wished to recommend him as a supervising official.

sentences.zh: 文祥曰：「昔以言事出，今以軍功進，不可。

translations.literal: Wenxiang said: 'Formerly I left office for remonstrance; now to advance on military merit—this cannot be.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang said, 'Formerly I left office for remonstrance; now to advance on military merit—that cannot be done.'

sentences.zh: 」固辭不得，乃請齎表入都，固乞告歸。

translations.literal: ' He firmly declined but could not succeed; then he requested to carry the memorial table to the capital and firmly begged leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: ' He firmly declined but could not succeed; then he requested permission to carry the memorial of tribute to the capital and firmly begged leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 疏再上，不許。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted again; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his request again, but it was not granted.

sentences.zh: 還經商城，渡冰陷，死焉，年僅三十。

translations.literal: Returning, he passed Shangcheng; crossing ice he fell through and died there, aged only thirty.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he passed through Shangcheng; crossing ice he fell through and drowned, aged only thirty.

sentences.zh: 孫磐，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Sun Pan was a man of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Pan was a native of Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 9 (1496) he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 觀政在部時，刑部典吏徐珪以滿倉兒事劾中官楊鵬得罪，磐上疏曰：「近諫官以言為諱，而排寵倖觸權奸者乃在胥吏，臣竊羞之。

translations.literal: While observing governance in the ministry, Criminal Section Clerk Xu Gui impeached inner official Yang Peng over the Mancang'er affair and was punished; Pan submitted a memorial saying: 'Recently remonstrating officials treat speech as taboo, yet those who oppose favored minions and touch powerful villains are found among clerks—your servant is privately ashamed.'
translations.idiomatic: While observing governance in the ministry, Criminal Section Clerk Xu Gui impeached the inner official Yang Peng over the Mancang'er affair and was punished; Pan submitted a memorial saying, 'Recently remonstrating officials treat speech as taboo, yet those who oppose favored minions and touch powerful villains are found among clerks—your servant is privately ashamed.'

sentences.zh: 請定建言者為四等。

translations.literal: I request fixing remonstrators in four grades.
translations.idiomatic: I request that remonstrators be classified in four grades.

sentences.zh: 最上不避患害，抗彈權貴者。

translations.literal: The highest grade: those who do not avoid calamity and harm, who resist and impeach the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: The highest grade: those who do not avoid calamity and harm and who resist and impeach the powerful and noble.

sentences.zh: 其次揚清激濁，能補闕拾遺。

translations.literal: The next: those who promote the pure and stir the turbid, able to supplement omissions and gather what was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The next grade: those who promote the pure and stir the turbid, able to supplement omissions and gather what was lost.

sentences.zh: 又其次，建白時政，有裨軍國。

translations.literal: Again the next: those who propose policies of the time, beneficial to military affairs and the state.
translations.idiomatic: Again the next: those who propose timely policies beneficial to military affairs and the state.

sentences.zh: 皆分別擢敘。

translations.literal: All are separately promoted and ranked.
translations.idiomatic: All should be separately promoted and ranked.

sentences.zh: 而粉飾文具、循默不言者，則罷黜之。

translations.literal: But those who adorn with documents and follow silence without speaking—then dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: But those who adorn themselves with empty documents and remain silent should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 庶言官知警，不至曠鳷。

translations.literal: Then remonstrating officials will know to be alert and will not reach the point of vacant magpies.
translations.idiomatic: Then remonstrating officials will know to be alert and will not stand vacant like magpies on a gate.

sentences.zh: 」時不見用。

translations.literal: ' At the time it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: 'At the time it was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 徐珪者，應城人。

translations.literal: Xu Gui was a man of Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui was a native of Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，千戶吳能以女滿倉兒付媒者鬻于樂婦張，紿曰：「周皇親家也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Battalion Commander Wu Neng gave his daughter Mancang'er to a matchmaker to sell to the procuress Zhang, deceiving her by saying: 'She is from the Zhou imperial relative's household.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Battalion Commander Wu Neng gave his daughter Mancang'er to a matchmaker to sell to the procuress Zhang, falsely claiming, 'She is from the household of the Zhou imperial relative.'

sentences.zh: 」後轉鬻樂工袁璘所。

translations.literal: ' Later she was resold to the musician Yuan Lin's place.
translations.idiomatic: ' Later she was resold to the musician Yuan Lin.

sentences.zh: 能歿，妻聶訪得之。

translations.literal: When Neng died, his wife Nie traced and found her.
translations.idiomatic: After Neng died, his wife Nie traced her whereabouts and found her.

sentences.zh: 女怨母鬻己，詭言非己母。

translations.literal: The daughter resented her mother for selling her and falsely said she was not her own mother.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter, resenting her mother for selling her, falsely claimed that Nie was not her mother.

sentences.zh: 聶與子劫女歸。

translations.literal: Nie and her son seized the daughter and took her back.
translations.idiomatic: Nie and her son seized the daughter and took her back by force.

sentences.zh: 璘訟于刑部，郎中丁哲、員外郎王爵訊得情。

translations.literal: Lin sued at the Ministry of Justice; Bureau Director Ding Zhe and Vice Bureau Director Wang Jue examined and got the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Lin sued at the Ministry of Justice; Bureau Director Ding Zhe and Vice Bureau Director Wang Jue examined the case and established the facts.

sentences.zh: 璘語不遜，哲笞璘，數日死。

translations.literal: Lin's words were not deferential; Zhe beat Lin with the bamboo, and within days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's words were insolent; Zhe beat him with the bamboo, and within days he died.

sentences.zh: 御史陳玉、主事孔琦驗璘屍，瘞之。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Yu and Section Chief Kong Qi examined Lin's corpse and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Yu and Section Chief Kong Qi examined Lin's corpse and had it buried.

sentences.zh: 東廠中官楊鵬從子嘗與女淫，教璘妻訴冤于鵬而令張指女為妹，又令賈校尉屬女亦如張言。

translations.literal: Eastern Depot inner official Yang Peng's nephew had once fornicated with the girl; he taught Lin's wife to plead injustice to Peng and had Zhang identify the girl as a younger sister, and also had Guard Captain Jia make the girl speak as Zhang had.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Peng, an inner official of the Eastern Depot, had a nephew who had once fornicated with the girl; he instructed Lin's wife to plead injustice to Peng, had Zhang identify the girl as a younger sister, and also had Guard Captain Jia instruct the girl to speak as Zhang had.

sentences.zh: 媒者遂言聶女前鬻周皇親矣。

translations.literal: The matchmaker then said that Nie's daughter had previously been sold to the Zhou imperial relative.
translations.idiomatic: The matchmaker then claimed that Nie's daughter had previously been sold to the Zhou imperial relative.

sentences.zh: 奏下鎮撫司，坐哲、爵等罪。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Brocade Guard Office; Zhe, Jue, and others were convicted.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent down to the Brocade Guard Office, and Zhe, Jue, and others were convicted.

sentences.zh: 復下法司、錦衣衛讞，索女皇親周彧家，無有。

translations.literal: Again sent down to the judicial offices and Brocade Guard for judgment; they searched the Zhou imperial relative Zhou Yu's household—there was none.
translations.idiomatic: The case was again sent down to the judicial offices and the Brocade Guard for judgment; they searched the household of the Zhou imperial relative Zhou Yu and found no such person.

sentences.zh: 復命府部大臣及給事、御史廷訊，張與女始吐實。

translations.literal: Again ordered ministers of the prefectures and ministries together with supervising secretaries and censors to examine at court; only then did Zhang and the girl begin to tell the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered ministers of the prefectures and ministries together with supervising secretaries and censors to examine the case at court; only then did Zhang and the girl begin to tell the truth.

sentences.zh: 都察院奏，哲因公杖人死，罪當徒。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized: Zhe, for beating a man to death in the course of official duty, should be punished with penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate memorialized that Zhe, for beating a man to death in the course of official duty, should be punished with penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 爵、玉、琦及聶母女當杖。

translations.literal: Jue, Yu, Qi, and Nie mother and daughter should be beaten with the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Jue, Yu, Qi, and Nie and her daughter should be beaten with the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 獄上，珪憤懣，抗疏曰：「聶女之獄，哲斷之審矣。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted, Gui was indignant and submitted a defiant memorial saying: 'In the case of Nie's daughter, Zhe judged it with thoroughness.'
translations.idiomatic: When the verdict was submitted, Gui, indignant, submitted a defiant memorial saying, 'In the case of Nie's daughter, Zhe judged it with thoroughness.'

sentences.zh: 鵬拷聶使誣服，鎮撫司共相蔽欺。

translations.literal: Peng tortured Nie to make her falsely confess; the Brocade Guard Office together deceived and covered it up.
translations.idiomatic: Peng tortured Nie to make her falsely confess, and the Brocade Guard Office together deceived and covered it up.

sentences.zh: 陛下令法司、錦衣會問，懼東廠莫敢明，至鞫之朝堂乃不能隱。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ordered the judicial offices and Brocade Guard to examine jointly, fearing the Eastern Depot none dared speak clearly; only at the court examination could it not be hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ordered the judicial offices and the Brocade Guard to examine the case jointly, but fearing the Eastern Depot none dared speak clearly; only at the court examination could the truth not be hidden.

sentences.zh: 夫女誣母僅擬杖，哲等無罪反加以徒。

translations.literal: The daughter falsely accusing her mother was only proposed for bamboo beating; Zhe and the others, though innocent, were instead given penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter who falsely accused her mother was only proposed for bamboo beating, while Zhe and the others, though innocent, were instead sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 輕重倒置如此，皆東廠威劫所致也。

translations.literal: Light and heavy inverted thus—all caused by the Eastern Depot's coercive power.
translations.idiomatic: Light and heavy thus inverted—all caused by the coercive power of the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 臣在刑部三年，見鞫問盜賊，多東廠鎮撫司緝獲，有稱校尉誣陷者，有稱校尉為人報仇者，有稱校尉受首惡贓而以為從、令傍人抵罪者。

translations.literal: Your servant was in the Ministry of Justice three years and saw interrogations of thieves and bandits—mostly captured by the Eastern Depot Brocade Guard Office; some said the guard captain falsely entrapped them, some said the guard captain avenged others, some said the guard captain received bribes from the chief villain and made accomplices and had bystanders bear guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant served in the Ministry of Justice for three years and saw interrogations of thieves and bandits—mostly cases captured by the Eastern Depot Brocade Guard Office; some said the guard captain had falsely entrapped them, some said the guard captain had avenged others, some said the guard captain had received bribes from the chief villain and made accomplices while having bystanders bear guilt.

sentences.zh: 刑官洞見其情，無敢擅更一字。

translations.literal: The criminal officials saw through the facts but dared not on their own change a single word.
translations.idiomatic: The criminal officials saw through the facts but dared not change a single word on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 上幹天和，災異迭見。

translations.literal: Above, it disturbs Heaven's harmony; calamities and anomalies appear in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Above, it disturbs Heaven's harmony; calamities and anomalies appear in successio.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下革去東廠，戮鵬叔侄並賈校尉及此女於市，謫戍鎮撫司官極邊，進哲、爵、琦、玉各一階，以洗其冤，則天意可回，太平可致。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to abolish the Eastern Depot, execute Peng and his nephew together with Guard Captain Jia and this girl in the marketplace, banish the Brocade Guard officials to the farthest border, and advance Zhe, Jue, Qi, and Yu each one rank—to wash away their injustice; then Heaven's intent can be turned back and great peace can be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to abolish the Eastern Depot, execute Peng and his nephew together with Guard Captain Jia and this girl in the marketplace, banish the Brocade Guard officials to the farthest border, and advance Zhe, Jue, Qi, and Yu each one rank—to clear their injustice; then Heaven's intent can be turned back and great peace can be attained.

sentences.zh: 如不罷東廠，亦當推選謹厚中官如陳寬、韋泰者居之，仍簡一大臣與共理。

translations.literal: If the Eastern Depot is not abolished, prudent and honest inner officials such as Chen Kuan and Wei Tai should be selected to preside, and a great minister should still be chosen to govern jointly.
translations.idiomatic: If the Eastern Depot is not abolished, prudent and honest inner officials such as Chen Kuan and Wei Tai should be selected to preside, and a senior minister should still be chosen to govern jointly.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫司理刑亦不宜專用錦衣官。

translations.literal: The Brocade Guard Office's administration of criminal cases also should not exclusively use Brocade Guard officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Brocade Guard Office's administration of criminal cases should also not rely exclusively on Brocade Guard officials.

sentences.zh: 乞推選在京各衛一二人及刑部主事一人，共蒞其事。

translations.literal: I beg to select one or two men from each guard in the capital together with one section chief from the Ministry of Justice to jointly preside over the matter.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that one or two men from each guard in the capital together with one section chief from the Ministry of Justice be selected to jointly preside over the matter.

sentences.zh: 或三年、六年一更，則巡捕官校，當有作奸擅刑，誣及無辜者矣。

translations.literal: If changed every three or six years, then the patrol-capture guard captains would sometimes commit fraud, abuse punishment, and falsely implicate the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: If rotated every three or six years, then the patrol-capture guard captains who commit fraud, abuse punishment, and falsely implicate the innocent would be exposed.

sentences.zh: 臣一介微軀，左右前後皆東廠鎮撫司之人，禍必不免。

translations.literal: Your servant is a single insignificant body; to left and right, before and behind, all are men of the Eastern Depot Brocade Guard Office—calamity cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is a single insignificant man; to left and right, before and behind, all are men of the Eastern Depot Brocade Guard Office—calamity cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 顧與其死於此輩，孰若死於朝廷。

translations.literal: Rather than die at the hands of such men, how much better to die at court.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than die at the hands of such men, how much better to die at the hands of the court.

sentences.zh: 願斬臣頭，以行臣言。

translations.literal: I wish to be beheaded to carry out my words.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to be beheaded so that my words may be carried out.

sentences.zh: 給臣妻子送骸骨歸，臣雖死無恨。

translations.literal: Grant my wife and children permission to send my bones home; though I die, I will have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Grant my wife and children permission to send my bones home; though I die, I will have no regre.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，下都察院考訊。

translations.literal: ' The emperor was angry and sent the case down to the Censorate for examination and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: 'The emperor was angry and sent the case down to the Censorate for examination and interrogation.

sentences.zh: 都御史閔珪等抵以奏事不實，贖徒還役。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Min Gui and others charged him with memorializing on matters not factual; he redeemed penal servitude and returned to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Min Gui and others charged him with memorializing on matters not factual; he redeemed penal servitude and returned to dut.

sentences.zh: 帝責具狀，皆上疏引罪，奪俸有差。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered detailed statements; all submitted memorials admitting guilt, and salaries were reduced by varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: This emperor ordered detailed statements; all submitted memorials admitting guilt, and salaries were reduced by varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 珪贖徒畢，發為民。

translations.literal: When Gui finished redeeming penal servitude, he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui finished redeeming penal servitude, he was dismissed to commoner statu.

sentences.zh: 既而給事中龐泮等言：「哲等獄詞覆奏已餘三月，系獄者凡三十八人，乞早為省釋。

translations.literal: Soon after, Supervising Secretary Pang Yang and others said: 'In the case of Zhe and others, the review of the prison testimony has already exceeded three months; those held in prison total thirty-eight persons—I beg early release for them.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Supervising Secretary Pang Yang and others said, 'In the case of Zhe and others, the review of the prison testimony has already exceeded three months; those held in prison total thirty-eight persons—I beg that they be released soon.'

sentences.zh: 」乃杖滿倉兒，送浣衣局。

translations.literal: ' Then Mancang'er was beaten with the bamboo and sent to the Laundry Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: 'Then Mancang'er was beaten with the bamboo and sent to the Laundry Bureau.

sentences.zh: 哲給璘理葬資，發為民。

translations.literal: Zhe provided funds for Lin's burial and was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe provided funds for Lin's burial and was dismissed to commoner statu.

sentences.zh: 爵及琦、玉俱贖杖還職。

translations.literal: Jue and Qi and Yu all redeemed bamboo beating and returned to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jue, Qi, and Yu all redeemed bamboo beating and returned to their posts.

sentences.zh: 時弘治九年十二月也。

translations.literal: It was the twelfth month of the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was the twelfth month of Hongzhi year 9 (1496).

sentences.zh: 珪以刑部主事陳鳳梧薦，授桐鄉丞。

translations.literal: On Criminal Section Chief Chen Fengwu's recommendation, Gui was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Tongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On Criminal Section Chief Chen Fengwu's recommendation, Gui was appointed assistant magistrate of Tongxiang.

sentences.zh: 正德中，曆贛州通判。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he served successively as Assistant Prefect of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he served successively as assistant prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 招降盜魁何積玉。

translations.literal: He induced the bandit chieftain He Jiyu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Then he induced the bandit chieftain He Jiyu to surrender.

sentences.zh: 已，復叛，下珪獄，尋釋之。

translations.literal: Later Jiyu rebelled again; Gui was imprisoned and soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiyu rebelled again; Gui was imprisoned and soon release.

sentences.zh: 後以平盜功擢知州。

translations.literal: Later, on merit in suppressing bandits, he was promoted to Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on merit in suppressing bandits, he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 胡爟，字仲光，蕪湖人。

translations.literal: Hu Guan, styled Zhongguang, was a man of Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guan, styled Zhongguang, was a native of Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 6 (1493) he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 改庶起士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: Transferred to a Hanlin Bachelor, he was appointed Section Chief in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed section chief in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，災異求言。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year, calamities and anomalies prompted a call for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year, calamities and anomalies prompted a call for remonstranc.

sentences.zh: 爟應詔，疏言：「中官李廣、楊鵬引左道劉良輔輩惑亂聖聰，濫設齋醮，耗蠹國儲。

translations.literal: Guan responded to the edict and memorialized saying: 'Inner officials Li Guang and Yang Peng brought in heterodox practitioners such as Liu Liangfu to bewilder the sage ear, wantonly establishing fasting and sacrifices, wasting and harming the national treasury.'
translations.idiomatic: Guan responded to the edict and memorialized saying, 'Inner officials Li Guang and Yang Peng brought in heterodox practitioners such as Liu Liangfu to bewilder the sage ear, wantonly establishing fasting and sacrifices, wasting and harming the national treasury.'

sentences.zh: 而不肖士大夫方昏暮乞憐於其門，交通請托。

translations.literal: Yet unworthy grand secretaries at dusk beg pity at their gates, exchanging communications and seeking favors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet unworthy grand secretaries at dusk beg for pity at their gates, exchanging communications and seeking favors.

sentences.zh: 陰盛陽微，災何由弭？

translations.literal: Yin flourishes and yang is weak—how can calamities be extinguished?
translations.idiomatic: Yin flourishes and yang is weak; how can calamities be extinguished?

sentences.zh: 」因極陳戚畹、方士、傳奉冗員之害。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he exhaustively set forth the harms of imperial in-laws, alchemists, and supernumerary transmitted appointees.
translations.idiomatic: 'Thereupon he exhaustively set forth the harms of imperial in-laws, alchemists, and supernumerary transmitted appointees.

sentences.zh: 疏留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was retained at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was retained at court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廣死，故爟得無罪。

translations.literal: Before long Guang died, and so Guan escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guang died, and so Guan escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，大同有警，命保國公硃暉禦之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, Datong had an alarm; the emperor ordered Defender of the State Duke Zhu Hui to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, Datong had an alarm; the emperor ordered Defender of the State Duke Zhu Hui to defend i.

sentences.zh: 行人永清王雄極言暉不足任，且請罷中官監督，以重將權。

translations.literal: Imperial Envoy Wang Xiong of Yongqing strongly stated that Hui was unfit for the task, and also requested abolishing inner eunuch supervision to strengthen the generals' authority.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Envoy Wang Xiong of Yongqing strongly stated that Hui was unfit for the task, and also requested abolishing palace eunuch supervision to strengthen the generals' authority.

sentences.zh: 苗逵方督暉軍，謂雄阻軍，乃下詔獄，謫雲南浪穹丞。

translations.literal: Miao Kui was then supervising Hui's army and said Xiong was obstructing the army; he was imprisoned by edict and demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Langqi in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Kui was then supervising Hui's army and said Xiong was obstructing the army; he was imprisoned by edict and demoted to assistant magistrate of Langqi in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 羅僑，字維升，吉水人。

translations.literal: Luo Qiao, styled Weisheng, was a man of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qiao, styled Weisheng, was a native of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 性純靜，寡嗜欲。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and quiet, with few desires.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was pure and quiet, with few desire.

sentences.zh: 受業張元禎，講學里中。

translations.literal: He studied under Zhang Yuanzhen and lectured on learning in the village.
translations.idiomatic: Then he studied under Zhang Yuanzhen and lectured on learning in the village.

sentences.zh: 舉弘治十二年進士，除新會知縣，有惠愛。

translations.literal: Selected as a jinshi in the twelfth year of Hongzhi, he was appointed Magistrate of Xinhui, with benevolence and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a jinshi in Hongzhi year 12 (1499), he was appointed magistrate of Xinhui, where he showed benevolence and kindness.

sentences.zh: 正德初，入為大理右評事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he entered service as Right Reviewing Censor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he entered service as right reviewing censor of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，京師旱霾，上疏曰：「臣聞人道理則陰陽和，政事失則災沴作。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, the capital suffered drought and haze; he submitted a memorial saying: 'Your servant has heard that when human affairs accord with principle, yin and yang are harmonious; when government affairs fail, calamities and anomalies arise.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year, the capital suffered drought and haze; he submitted a memorial saying, 'Your servant has heard that when human affairs accord with principle, yin and yang are harmonious; when government affairs fail, calamities and anomalies arise.'

sentences.zh: 頃因京師久旱，陛下特沛德音，釋逋戍之囚，弛株連之禁，而齋禱經旬，雨澤尚滯。

translations.literal: Recently, because the capital had long suffered drought, Your Majesty specially issued a benevolent edict, releasing prisoners with overdue sentences and relaxing punishments of collective guilt, yet after fasting and prayer for ten days rain still lagged.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because the capital had long suffered drought, the emperor specially issued a benevolent edict, releasing prisoners with overdue sentences and relaxing punishments of collective guilt, yet after fasting and prayer for ten days rain still lagged.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為天心仁愛未已也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that Heaven's heart of benevolent love has not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately believes that Heaven's heart of benevolent love has not yet ceased.

sentences.zh: 陛下視朝，或至日昃，狎侮群小，號呶達旦，其何以承天心基大業乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty holds court, sometimes until the sun slants west; you dally with petty men and shout and clamor until dawn—how can you receive Heaven's heart and establish the great enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds court, sometimes until the sun slants west; you dally with petty men and shout and clamor until dawn—how can you receive Heaven's heart and establish the great enterprise?

sentences.zh: 文網日密，誅求峻急。

translations.literal: The net of literary punishments grows daily tighter; exactions and demands are severe and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: This net of literary punishments grows daily tighter; exactions and demands are severe and urgent.

sentences.zh: 盜賊白晝殺人，百姓流移載道，元氣索然。

translations.literal: Bandits kill people in broad daylight; the common people flee and migrate, filling the roads; vital energy is utterly depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits kill people in broad daylight; the common people flee and migrate, filling the roads; vital energy is utterly deplete.

sentences.zh: 科道知之而不敢言，內閣言之而不敢盡，此壅蔽之大患也。

translations.literal: The censorate and remonstrance officials know this but dare not speak; the Grand Secretariat speaks but dare not speak fully—this is the great evil of obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate and remonstrance officials know this but dare not speak; the Grand Secretariat speaks but dare not speak fully—this is the great evil of obstruction.

sentences.zh: 古者進退大臣，必有體貌，黥劓之罪不上大夫。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when advancing or dismissing great ministers there was always proper ceremony; tattooing and nose-cutting punishments did not reach grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when advancing or dismissing great ministers there was always proper ceremony; tattooing and nose-cutting punishments did not reach grand secretarie.

sentences.zh: 邇來公卿去不以禮。

translations.literal: Recently grand secretaries and ministers have departed without ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Recently grand secretaries and ministers have departed without ceremon.

sentences.zh: 先朝忠藎如劉大夏者，謫戍窮邊，已及三載，陛下置之不問，非所以待耆舊、敬大臣也。

translations.literal: Formerly loyal and steadfast men of the previous reign such as Liu Daxia were banished to the farthest border for nearly three years; Your Majesty has left them unattended—this is not how to treat elders and respect great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly loyal and steadfast men of the previous reign such as Liu Daxia were banished to the farthest border for nearly three years; the emperor has left them unattended—this is not how to treat elders and respect great ministers.

sentences.zh: 本朝律例，參酌古今，足以懲奸而蔽罪。

translations.literal: The statutes and precedents of this dynasty, drawn from past and present, are sufficient to punish the wicked and cover crimes.
translations.idiomatic: This statutes and precedents of this dynasty, drawn from past and present, are sufficient to punish the wicked and cover crimes.

sentences.zh: 近者法司承望風旨，巧中善類。

translations.literal: Recently the judicial offices have followed the wind of intent and artfully struck good men.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the judicial offices have followed the wind of intent and artfully struck good me.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『賞僭則及淫人，刑濫則及善人。

translations.literal: The Classic says: 'If rewards are excessive, they reach licentious men; if punishments are excessive, they reach good men.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says, 'If rewards are excessive, they reach licentious men; if punishments are excessive, they reach good men.'

sentences.zh: 不幸而過，寧僭無濫。

translations.literal: If one must err, better excessive reward than excessive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If one must err, better excessive reward than excessive punishmen.

sentences.zh: 』今之刑罰，濫孰甚焉。

translations.literal: ' Today's punishments—what excess could be greater?
translations.idiomatic: 'Today's punishments—what excess could be greater?

sentences.zh: 願陛下慎逸游，屏玩好，放棄小人，召還舊德，與在廷臣工，宵旰圖治，並敕法司慎守成律。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to be careful of idle wandering, to put aside amusements, to abandon petty men, to recall old virtue, together with ministers at court to toil day and night in seeking good governance, and also to order the judicial offices carefully to keep the established statutes.
translations.idiomatic: I wish the emperor to be careful of idle wandering, to put aside amusements, to abandon petty men, to recall old virtue, together with ministers at court to toil day and night in seeking good governance, and also to order the judicial offices carefully to keep the established statutes.

sentences.zh: 即有律輕情重者，亦必奏請裁決，毋擅有輕重。

translations.literal: Even if the statute is light and the circumstances heavy, it must also be submitted for imperial decision—do not on your own authority have light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the statute is light and the circumstances heavy, it must also be submitted for imperial decision—do not on your own authority vary the severity.

sentences.zh: 庶可上弭天變，下收人心。

translations.literal: Then above you can extinguish Heaven's changes and below gather people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Then above you can extinguish Heaven's changes and below gather people's heart.

sentences.zh: 」時朝士久以言為諱。

translations.literal: ' At the time court gentlemen had long treated speech as taboo.
translations.idiomatic: 'At the time court gentlemen had long treated speech as taboo.

sentences.zh: 僑疏上，自揣必死，輿櫬待命。

translations.literal: When Qiao's memorial was submitted, he reckoned he would surely die and carried a coffin awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiao's memorial was submitted, he reckoned he would surely die and carried a coffin awaiting order.

sentences.zh: 臣願廣開言路，勿罪其出位，勿責其沽名，將忠言日進，聰明日廣，亂臣賊子亦有所畏而不敢肆矣。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes broadly to open the path of speech, not to punish overstepping rank, not to charge with seeking fame—then loyal words will daily advance, wisdom daily broaden, and treacherous ministers and wicked sons will also have something to fear and not dare act wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: I wishes broadly to open the path of speech, not to punish overstepping rank, not to charge with seeking fame—then loyal words will daily advance, wisdom daily broaden, and treacherous ministers and wicked sons will also have something to fear and not dare act wantonly.

sentences.zh: 三，正名號。

translations.literal: Third, correct titles and designations.
translations.idiomatic: Third, correct titles and designations. So it was.

sentences.zh: 陛下無故降稱大將軍、太師、鎮國公，遠近傳聞，莫不驚歎。

translations.literal: Your Majesty without reason lowered titles of Great General, Grand Preceptor, and Defender of the State; near and far heard it and none were not startled and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty without reason assumed the titles of Great General, Grand Preceptor, and Defender of the State; near and far, all who heard it were startled and dismayed.

sentences.zh: 如此，則誰為天子者？

translations.literal: In this way, who is the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: In this way, who is the Son of Heaven? So it was.

sentences.zh: 天下不以天子事陛下，而以將軍事陛下，天下皆為將軍之臣矣。

translations.literal: The realm does not serve Your Majesty as Son of Heaven but as general; the realm all become the general's ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The realm does not serve the emperor as Son of Heaven but as general; the realm all become the general's ministers.

sentences.zh: 今不削去諸名號，昭上下之分，則體統不正，朝廷不尊。

translations.literal: Now if you do not cut away these titles and designations and clarify the distinction of above and below, then the institutional order is not correct and the court is not honored.
translations.idiomatic: Now if you do not cut away these titles and designations and clarify the distinction of above and below, then the institutional order is not correct and the court is not honore.

sentences.zh: 古之天子亦有號稱「獨夫」，求為匹夫而不得者，竊為陛下懼焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity even the Son of Heaven had the title 'Lone Man'; some sought to be commoners and could not—your servant privately fears for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity even the Son of Heaven had the title 'Lone Man'; some sought to be commoners and could not—your servant privately fears for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 四，戒遊幸。

translations.literal: Fourth, guard against touring.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, guard against touring. So it was.

sentences.zh: 陛下始時遊戲，不出大庭，馳逐止于南內，論者猶謂不可。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first played, you did not leave the great hall; racing and chasing stopped at the Southern Inner Palace—discussants still said it was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first played, you did not leave the great hall; racing and chasing stopped at the Southern Inner Palace—discussants still said it was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 既而幸宣府矣，幸大同矣，幸太原、榆林矣。

translations.literal: Then you favored Xuanfu, favored Datong, favored Taiyuan and Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Then you favored Xuanfu, favored Datong, favored Taiyuan and Yuli.

sentences.zh: 所至費財動眾，郡縣騷然，至使民間夫婦不相保。

translations.literal: Wherever you arrived you wasted wealth and moved crowds; prefectures and counties were disturbed, until husbands and wives among the people could not protect each other.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever you arrived you wasted wealth and moved crowds; prefectures and counties were disturbed, until husbands and wives among the people could not protect each othe.

sentences.zh: 陛下為民父母，何忍使至此極也？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people—how can you bear to bring them to this extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people—how can you bear to bring them to this extreme?

sentences.zh: 近復有南巡之命。

translations.literal: Recently there was again an order for a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: Recently there was again an order for a southern tou.

sentences.zh: 南方之民爭先挈妻子避去，流離奔踣，怨讟煩興。

translations.literal: People of the south competed to take wives and children and flee; wandering in exile and falling prostrate, resentment and curses arose in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: People of the south competed to take wives and children and flee; wandering in exile and falling prostrate, resentment and curses arose in abundanc.

sentences.zh: 今江、淮大饑，父子兄弟相食。

translations.literal: Now the Yangzi and Huai regions suffer great famine; fathers and sons and brothers eat one another.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Yangzi and Huai regions suffer great famine; fathers and sons and brothers eat one anothe.

sentences.zh: 天時人事如此，陛下又重蹙之，幾何不流為盜賊也。

translations.literal: Heaven's season and human affairs being thus, Your Majesty again heavily presses them—how will they not turn into bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's season and human affairs being thus, the emperor again heavily presses them—how will they not turn into bandits?

sentences.zh: 奸雄窺伺，侍時而發。

translations.literal: Treacherous heroes watch and wait, awaiting the moment to act.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous heroes watch and wait, awaiting the moment to ac.

sentences.zh: 變生在內，則欲歸無路；

translations.literal: If change arises within, then you wish to return but there is no way;
translations.idiomatic: If change arises within, then you wish to return but there is no way; So it was.

sentences.zh: 變生在外，則望救無及。

translations.literal: if change arises without, then you hope for rescue but it cannot arrive.
translations.idiomatic: If disaster arises outside, you will hope for rescue but none can arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 陛下斯時，悔之晚矣。

translations.literal: At that time, Your Majesty, it will be too late for regret.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the emperor, it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 彼居位大臣，用事中官，親昵群小，夫豈有毫髮愛陛下之心哉？

translations.literal: Those great ministers in office, inner eunuchs in power, and intimate petty men—do they have even a hair's worth of love for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Those great ministers in office, inner eunuchs in power, and intimate petty men—do they have even a hair's worth of love for the emperor?

sentences.zh: 皆欲陛下遠出，而後得以擅權自恣，乘機為利也。

translations.literal: All wish Your Majesty to go far out so that afterward they can usurp power at will and seize opportunity for profit.
translations.idiomatic: All wish the emperor to go far out so that afterward they can usurp power at will and seize opportunity for profit.

sentences.zh: 其不然，則亦袖手旁觀，如秦、越人不相休戚也。

translations.literal: If not, they fold their arms and watch from the side, like men of Qin and Yue who do not share each other's joy and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: If not, they fold their arms and watch from the side, like men of Qin and Yue who do not share each other's joy and sorro.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜翻然悔悟，下哀痛罪己之詔。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should suddenly repent, and issue an edict of sorrowful pain confessing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should repent at once and issue an edict of sorrowful self-reproach confessing guilt.

sentences.zh: 罷南巡，撤宣府離宮，示不復出。

translations.literal: Cancel the southern tour, withdraw the Xuanfu detached palace, and show you will not go out again.
translations.idiomatic: Cancel the southern tour, withdraw the Xuanfu detached palace, and show you will not go out agai.

sentences.zh: 發內帑以振江、淮，散邊軍以歸卒伍。

translations.literal: Release inner treasury funds to relieve the Yangzi and Huai, and disperse frontier troops to return to the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Release inner treasury funds to relieve the Yangzi and Huai, and disperse frontier troops to return to the rank.

sentences.zh: 雪已往之謬舉，收既失之人心。

translations.literal: Clear away past mistaken actions and recover lost popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Clear away past mistaken actions and recover lost popular heart.

sentences.zh: 如是，則尚可為也。

translations.literal: If so, then there is still hope.
translations.idiomatic: If so, then there is still hope. So it was.

sentences.zh: 五，去小人。

translations.literal: Fifth, remove petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, remove petty men. So it was.

sentences.zh: 自古未有小人用事不亡國喪身者也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity there has never been petty men in power without ruining the state and losing one's life.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity there has never been petty men in power without ruining the state and losing one's lif.

sentences.zh: 今之小人簸弄威權、貪溺富貴者，實繁有徒。

translations.literal: Today's petty men who manipulate authority and greedily drown in wealth and honor are indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: Today's petty men who manipulate authority and greedily drown in wealth and honor are indeed man.

sentences.zh: 至於首開邊事，以兵為戲，使陛下勞天下之力，竭四海之財，傷百姓之心者，則江彬之為也。

translations.literal: As for first opening frontier affairs and treating war as play, making Your Majesty toil the realm's strength, exhaust the four seas' wealth, and wound the people's hearts—that was Jiang Bin's doing.
translations.idiomatic: As for first opening frontier affairs and treating war as play, making the emperor toil the realm's strength, exhaust the four seas' wealth, and wound the people's hearts—that was Jiang Bin's doing.

sentences.zh: 彬，行伍庸流，兇狠傲誕，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Bin is a common soldier of low origin, fierce and arrogant beyond measure, without the rites of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Bin is a common soldier of low origin, fierce and arrogant beyond measure, without the rites of a ministe.

sentences.zh: 臣但見其有可誅之罪，不聞其有可賞之功。

translations.literal: Your servant only sees crimes deserving execution, not merit deserving reward.
translations.idiomatic: I only sees crimes deserving execution, not merit deserving reward.

sentences.zh: 今乃賜以國姓，封以伯爵，托以心腹，付以京營重寄。

translations.literal: Now he is granted the imperial surname, enfeoffed as earl, entrusted as confidant, and given the heavy charge of the Capital Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is granted the imperial surname, enfeoffed as earl, entrusted as confidant, and given the heavy charge of the Capital Garriso.

sentences.zh: 使其外持兵柄，內蓄逆謀，以成騎虎之勢，此必亂之道也。

translations.literal: Making him outwardly hold military power and inwardly harbor treacherous designs to form the situation of riding a tiger—this is the way that must lead to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Making him outwardly hold military power and inwardly harbor treacherous designs to form the situation of riding a tiger; this is the way that must lead to disorder.

sentences.zh: 天下切齒怒駡，皆欲食彬之肉。

translations.literal: The realm grinds teeth in anger and curses, all wishing to eat Bin's flesh.
translations.idiomatic: This realm grinds teeth in anger and curses, all wishing to eat Bin's flesh.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦何惜一彬，不以謝天下哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty, why spare one Bin and not apologize to the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, why spare one Bin and not apologize to the realm?

sentences.zh: 六，建儲貳。

translations.literal: Sixth, establish the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, establish the heir apparent. So it was.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋漸高，前星未耀，祖宗社稷之托搖搖無所寄。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years gradually advance; the former star has not yet shone; the trust of the ancestors' altars and state hangs unsettled with nowhere to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's years gradually advance; the heir apparent has not yet shone; the trust of the ancestors' altars and state hangs unsettled with nowhere to rest.

sentences.zh: 方且遠事觀遊，屢犯不測；

translations.literal: Yet you far pursue sightseeing and repeatedly venture into the unknown;
translations.idiomatic: Yet you far pursue sightseeing and repeatedly venture into the unknown; So it was.

sentences.zh: 收養義子，佈滿左右。

translations.literal: you adopt foster sons and spread them throughout those at your side.
translations.idiomatic: You adopt foster sons and spread them throughout those at your side.

sentences.zh: 獨不能豫建親賢以承大業，臣以為陛下殆倒置也。

translations.literal: Alone you cannot beforehand establish a close and worthy heir to inherit the great enterprise—your servant considers that Your Majesty has almost inverted priorities.
translations.idiomatic: Alone you cannot beforehand establish a close and worthy heir to inherit the great enterprise—your servant considers that the emperor has almost inverted priorities.

sentences.zh: 伏望上告宗廟，請命太后，旁諏大臣，擇宗室親賢者一人養于宮中，以系四海之望。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly hopes to report above to the ancestral temple, request orders from the empress dowager, consult widely with great ministers, choose one close and worthy member of the imperial clan to nurture in the palace to bind the hope of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hopes to report above to the ancestral temple, request orders from the empress dowager, consult widely with great ministers, choose one close and worthy member of the imperial clan to nurture in the palace to bind the hope of the four seas.

sentences.zh: 他日誕生皇子，仍俾出籓，實宗社無疆之福也。

translations.literal: If another day a prince is born, still let him go out to the fief—it is truly boundless fortune for the altars and state.
translations.idiomatic: If another day a prince is born, still let him go out to the fief; it is truly boundless fortune for the altars and state.

sentences.zh: 員外郎陸震草疏將諫，見鞏疏稱歎，因毀己稿，與鞏連署以進。

translations.literal: Vice Bureau Director Lu Zhen had drafted a memorial to remonstrate; seeing Gong's memorial he praised it, destroyed his own draft, and joined Gong in submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Bureau Director Lu Zhen had drafted a memorial to remonstrate; seeing Gong's memorial he praised it, destroyed his own draft, and joined Gong in submittin.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，下二人詔獄，復跪午門。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent both men to prison by edict; they again knelt at the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: This emperor was greatly angered and sent both men to prison by edict; they again knelt at the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 眾謂天子且出，鞏曰：「天子出，吾當牽裾死之。

translations.literal: The crowd said the Son of Heaven would come out; Gong said: 'When the Son of Heaven comes out, I shall seize his robe and die.'
translations.idiomatic: The crowd said the Son of Heaven would come out; Gong said, 'When the Son of Heaven comes out, I shall seize his robe and die.'

sentences.zh: 」跪五日，期滿，仍系獄。

translations.literal: They knelt five days; when the term expired they were still imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: They knelt five days; when the term expired they were still imprisone.

sentences.zh: 越二十餘日，廷杖五十，斥為民。

translations.literal: After more than twenty days they were beaten with the club fifty times and dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days they received beating with the club fifty times and dismissed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 彬使人沿途刺鞏，有治洪主事知而匿之，間行得脫。

translations.literal: Bin sent men to assassinate Gong along the route; Section Chief Hong of Zhihong knew and hid him; traveling by side paths he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent men to assassinate Gong along the route; section chief Hong of Zhihong knew and hid him; traveling by side paths he escaped.

sentences.zh: 既歸，潛心著述。

translations.literal: After returning he devoted himself to writing.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he devoted himself to writin.

sentences.zh: 或米盡，日中未爨，晏如也。

translations.literal: Sometimes when rice was exhausted, at midday he had not yet cooked, yet he was calm.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when rice was exhausted, at midday he had not yet cooked, yet he was cal.

sentences.zh: 嘗歎曰：「人生至公卿富貴矣，然不過三四十年。

translations.literal: He once sighed: 'In life one reaches grand secretaries and wealth and honor—but that is only three or four decades.'
translations.idiomatic: He once sighed, 'In life one reaches grand secretaries and wealth and honor—but that is only three or four decades.'

sentences.zh: 惟立身行道，千載不朽。

translations.literal: Only establishing oneself and practicing the Way lasts a thousand ages without decay.
translations.idiomatic: Only establishing oneself and practicing the Way lasts a thousand ages without deca.

sentences.zh: 世人顧往往以此易彼，何也？」

translations.literal: Worldly people often exchange this for that—why?'
translations.idiomatic: Worldly people often exchange this for that; why?'

sentences.zh: 世宗立，召為南京大理丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded he was summoned as Assistant Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded he was summoned as assistant director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 疏請稽古正學，敬天勤民，取則堯、舜，保全君子，辯別小人。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to examine antiquity and correct learning, revere Heaven and toil for the people, take Yao and Shun as models, preserve gentlemen and distinguish petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Then he memorialized requesting to examine antiquity and correct learning, revere Heaven and toil for the people, take Yao and Shun as models, preserve gentlemen and distinguish petty men.

sentences.zh: 明年入賀，卒于京師。

translations.literal: The next year he entered to offer congratulations and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: This next year he entered to offer congratulations and died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 行人張岳訟其直節，贈大理少卿，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: Imperial Envoy Zhang Yue pleaded his upright integrity; he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and granted sacrificial burial.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Envoy Zhang Yue pleaded his upright integrity; he was posthumously granted vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and granted sacrificial burial.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追諡忠裕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously granted the posthumous name Zhongyu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the posthumous name Zhongyu.

sentences.zh: 陸震，字汝亭，蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhen, styled Ruting, was a man of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhen, styled Ruting, was a native of Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 受業同縣章懋，以學行知名。

translations.literal: He studied under Zhang Mao of the same county and was known for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Then he studied under Zhang Mao of the same county and was known for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 3 (1508) he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 除泰和知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 時劉瑾擅政。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Jin monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Jin monopolized government.

sentences.zh: 以逋鹽課責縣民償者連數百人，震力白之上官，得免。

translations.literal: Because of overdue salt tax several hundred county people were charged to repay; Zhen forcefully explained to superiors and they were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Because of overdue salt tax several hundred county people were charged to repay; Zhen forcefully explained to superiors and they were exempte.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官歲征貢絺，為減其額。

translations.literal: The defending inner eunuch annually levied tribute silk; he reduced the quota.
translations.idiomatic: The defending palace eunuch annually levied tribute silk; he reduced the quota.

sentences.zh: 增築學舍居諸生，毀淫祠祀忠節。

translations.literal: He expanded the schoolhouse to house students and destroyed licentious shrines to sacrifice to loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Then he expanded the schoolhouse to house students and destroyed licentious shrines to sacrifice to loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 浮糧累民，稽賦籍，得詭寄隱匿者萬五千石以補之。

translations.literal: Floating grain burdened the people; he examined tax registers and found concealed and hidden registrations of fifteen thousand shi to supplement them.
translations.idiomatic: Floating grain burdened the people; he examined tax registers and found concealed and hidden registrations of fifteen thousand shi to supplement the.

sentences.zh: 建倉縣左，儲穀待振。

translations.literal: He built granaries to the left of the county and stored grain awaiting relief.
translations.idiomatic: Then he built granaries to the left of the county and stored grain awaiting relief.

sentences.zh: 親行鄉落，勸課農桑。

translations.literal: He personally walked the villages and urged agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Then he personally walked the villages and urged agriculture and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 立保伍法，使民備盜。

translations.literal: He established the mutual-responsibility law to make the people guard against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Then he established the mutual-responsibility law to make the people guard against bandits.

sentences.zh: 甓城七里，外為土城十里周之。

translations.literal: He tiled the city wall for seven li and surrounded it outside with an earthen wall of ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Then he tiled the city wall for seven li and surrounded it outside with an earthen wall of ten li.

sentences.zh: 時發狼兵討賊，所至擾民。

translations.literal: At the time wolf troops were dispatched to suppress bandits and wherever they arrived they disturbed the people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time wolf troops were dispatched to suppress bandits and wherever they arrived they disturbed the people.

sentences.zh: 震言于總督，令毋聽檥舟，官具糧糗，以次續食，兵行肅然。

translations.literal: Zhen spoke to the governor-general, ordering them not to moor boats; officials supplied grain and rations and food was supplied in succession—the troops marched in order.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen spoke to the governor-general, ordering them not to moor boats; officials supplied grain and rations and food was supplied in succession; the troops marched in order.

sentences.zh: 督捕永豐、新淦賊，以功受賞。

translations.literal: Supervising the capture of bandits in Yongfeng and Xingan, he received reward for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising the capture of bandits in Yongfeng and Xingan, he received reward for meri.

sentences.zh: 撫按交薦，征為兵部主事。

translations.literal: The governor and censor jointly recommended him; he was summoned as Section Chief in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The governor and censor jointly recommended him; he was summoned as section chief in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 泰和人生祠之。

translations.literal: The people of Taihe built a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: This people of Taihe built a living shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 在部，主諸司章奏，與中人忤，改巡紫荊諸關。

translations.literal: In the ministry he managed memorials of all bureaus; he clashed with inner eunuchs and was changed to inspect the Cercis Passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ministry he managed memorials of all bureaus; he clashed with inner eunuchs and was changed to inspect the Cercis Passe.

sentences.zh: 又以論都御史彭澤、副使胡世寧無罪，忤尚書王瓊、陸完。

translations.literal: Again because he argued that Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze and Vice Commissioner Hu Shining were innocent, he clashed with Ministers Wang Qiong and Lu Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Again because he argued that Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze and Vice Commissioner Hu Shining were innocent, he clashed with Ministers Wang Qiong and Lu Wa.

sentences.zh: 孝貞皇后崩，武宗至自宣府。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaozhen died, Emperor Wuzong returned from Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaozhen died, Emperor Wuzong returned from Xuanf.

sentences.zh: 既發喪數日，復欲北出。

translations.literal: Having departed mourning for several days, he again wished to go north.
translations.idiomatic: Having departed mourning for several days, he again wished to go nort.

sentences.zh: 震抗疏曰：「日者，昊天不吊，威降大戚。

translations.literal: Zhen submitted a defiant memorial saying: 'Recently, Heaven did not pity us and sent down great sorrow.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhen submitted a defiant memorial saying, 'Recently, Heaven did not pity us and sent down great sorrow.'

sentences.zh: 車駕在狩，群情惶惶。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was on the hunt; popular sentiment was anxious.
translations.idiomatic: This imperial carriage was on the hunt; popular sentiment was anxious.

sentences.zh: 陛下單騎沖雪還宮，百官有司莫不感愴，以為陛下前蔽而今明也。

translations.idiomatic: Their clashing with powerful favorites, pointing at and rebuking the imperial carriage, all cut to the utmost plans of safety and dange.

sentences.zh: 若張英陷胸以悟主，徐鏊托術以諷諭，誠心出於忠愛，抑尤人所難能者矣。

translations.literal: If Zhang Ying pierced his chest to awaken his lord, and Xu Ao relied on his art to admonish by indirection—their sincere hearts arose from loyal love, and these were especially what others find hard to accomplish.
